chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-Is ibn al-Qasim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I had lunch with him, so he said to me: 'Do you know what this is?' I said, 'No'. He said: 'This is Shiraz al-Atun (a type of yogurt drink). We have prepared it for one of our sick people, so if you wish to eat from it, then eat.'

key_terms.تَغَدَّيْتُ: I had lunch / I ate the midday meal
key_terms.شِيرَازُ الْأُتُنِ: Shiraz al-Atun, a specific type of yogurt drink or lassi
key_terms.لِمَرِيضٍ لَنَا: For one of our sick people

ai.seo_question: What is Shiraz al-Atun and how was it used by the Imams?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the practical wisdom of consuming 'Shiraz al-Atun' (a yogurt-based drink) for medicinal purposes, specifically for the ill, reflecting the Shia tradition of integrating dietary health with spiritual life. The Imam’s casual invitation to his companion underscores the permissibility and virtue of sharing simple, nourishing foods in a spirit of hospitality and communal care.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Abdul Rahma Bin Abu Najran, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from l Ays Bin Al Qasim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I had lunch with him<sup>asws</sup>, so he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘Do you know what this is?’ I said, ‘No’.
Heasws said: ‘Sheyraz Al-Atun.  Weasws take it for ourasws sick, so Iasws would love it if you would eat from it’. So I ate’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn abu ibn abu Najran from Safwan ibn Yahya from al-‘Is ibn al-Qasim who has said the following: “

I once had lunch with abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, and he (the Imam) said to me, ‘Do you know what this is?’ I replied, ‘No, I do not know. 5 He (the Imam) said, ‘This is Shiraz al-’Utun (yogurt- water) that we have extracted for one of our patients. If you like to eat you can eat it.’”
